producer.plain_char_target_result: For this pinned MSC 6.00AX target and flags, plain char is sign-extended: generated LoadMonoPats assembly loads the header byte to AL, executes CBW, then SHL AX,CL with CL=3. The plain-char fixture emits CBW; signed-char control also emits CBW; unsigned-char control clears AH with SUB AH,AH.
producer.loop_result: The generated LoadMonoPats loop initializes i=0 and compares i against n with signed JL. For a header byte 0x00..0x7F, n=8*v in [0,1016], so the copy writes exactly offsets [0,8*v), at most 1016 bytes (last byte offset 1015). For 0x80..0xFF, machine sign extension followed by the 16-bit shift yields -1024..-8; the emitted signed loop comparison is false at i=0, so the target instruction sequence copies zero bytes.
producer.source_language_caveat: Left-shifting a negative promoted signed char has no portable C guarantee; the high-bit case above is an inference from the pinned compiler-emitted 8086 instruction sequence, not a source-level contract.
producer.resource_bound: The requested (object 0x271A, kind 0x16) header/payload is absent from the available supplied resource set per the existing monochrome owner-gap evidence; therefore the header byte domain actually produced at runtime is unknown. The conditional compiler bound does not close that gate.
producer.assembly_pin: S15CAN.ASM lines 213-220 show byte load/CBW/shift; lines 229-252 show zero-initialized loop index and signed JL against n.

combined_conclusion.consumer_possible_index_range: S01 source bytes are zero-extended before multiplying by 8; byte values 0..255 and selector values 0..7 permit per-read displacements up to 0x0802 (three-lane routines) and 0x0800 (one-lane routines).
combined_conclusion.producer_vs_consumer: The maximum positive producer copy from a nonnegative signed-char header is 1016 bytes, while S01 arithmetic permits byte reads through displacement 2050/2048. No evidence here bounds the row byte values or proves all reads covered by the producer copy.
